relevance_note: The paper reports an infant with a TNFAIP3 nonsense variant ("NM_006290.3:c.492G>A (p.Trp164Ter)") and her father, both with HA20.
method_note: Read the paper only. I transcribed all quotes by hand from the Markdown, checking each string with a search of the file; no script was used. Tables 1 and 2 are single-patient laboratory tables with no patient label; their cells are therefore attributed to the one patient, the infant. Labels: the paper uses no per-person labels, so I used relation-based labels (rule 2) 'father of the infant', 'mother of the infant', 'grandmother of the infant' and rule 5 'infant' for the single case-report patient (the paper calls her 'the proband' in Fig. 2, a role word, so rule 1 does not apply). Contradictions found: (1) the variant is called 'a definite pathogenic mutation' in the case description but 'likely pathogenic variant nonsense mutations in the TNFAIP3 gene' in the Discussion; pathogenicity_as_stated_by_authors keeps the 'definite pathogenic mutation' wording and the second statement is noted here. (2) The abstract says the father's symptoms 'including oral and genital ulcers, knee arthralgia, abdominal pain, and diarrhea', matching the body text. (3) The Discussion says 'she tested negative for maternal autoantibodies', while line 63 states that several laboratory tests for autoantibodies in the mother 'were all negative'; I did not record a feature for this ambiguous statement. (4) The NF1 variant is printed as 'heterozygote'; the zygosity enum value 'heterozygous' is used with the paper's word in the span. Note that Table 1 lists anti-Ro as 'Positive' and anti-La as 'Borderline' at 2 months of age, which could be transplacental maternal antibodies; I did not record those as the infant's features and used the ANA result and the Discussion statement about her own autoantibodies instead. Study scope: the study states no overall cohort size (single case report), and the total number of patients with a TNFAIP3 variant described is 2 (the infant and her father). Two further judgement calls: (a) the infant's height is reported as 'approximately three percentiles', which I recorded as a phenotypic feature but did NOT convert into the checklist item 'growth failure' (no explicit statement of growth failure, and weight was around 25 percentiles); (b) I did not record 'low C3 and C4' as a feature even though Table 1 prints C3 48 mg/dL and C4 < 2 mg/dL, because no reference range is printed and the paper only says 'Levels of C3 and C4 improved'; the complement item is not in the checklist, so nothing is lost there. For the checklist I marked 'uveitis or other ocular inflammation' excluded for the infant, because the paper names ocular inflammation directly; I left 'arthritis or arthralgia' not reported, since the paper excludes arthritis only (a narrower absence does not exclude the broader item).
